overview: This Senate resolution marks the 80th anniversary, on May 14, 2025, of continuous operations of Stars and Stripes in the Pacific. Stars and Stripes is a newspaper for the U.S. military community that first appeared during the Civil War and became permanent during World War II, when its Pacific edition was launched in Honolulu to give troops independent news; it began printing in Tokyo in October 1945. The resolution notes that it has covered every major U.S. conflict since and now reaches readers online as well as in print. It congratulates and honors the people who have worked for the paper. It is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on December 9, 2025.
for: Supporters say Stars and Stripes has long given service members and their families overseas reliable news from home, and its history deserves recognition.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, policy, or funding for the newspaper.
